Expanded and arrival matrices

Source: vignettes/articles/expanded-and-arrival.Rmd
expanded-and-arrival.Rmd

travel_time_matrix() reduces the trips of a departure window to a few percentiles. Two functions keep the trips themselves: expanded_travel_time_matrix() returns every one, and arrival_travel_time_matrix() the one that leaves latest and still arrives in time. Both work with public transport (mode = c("WALK", "TRANSIT")).

Every trip 

trips <- expanded_travel_time_matrix(
  network, points[1:2, ], points,
  mode = c("WALK", "TRANSIT"),
  departure_datetime = departure,
  time_window = 3,
  breakdown = TRUE,
  seed = 42,
  n_threads = 2
)
nrow(trips) == 2 * nrow(points) * 3 * 5
#> [1] TRUE
head(subset(trips, routes != "[WALK]"), 10)
#> # A tibble: 10 × 12
#>    from_id      to_id departure_time draw_number access_time wait_time ride_time
#>    <chr>        <chr> <chr>                <int>       <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>
#>  1 89a8100c00f… 89a8… 14:01:00                 1        16.1       1.4       2.2
#>  2 89a8100c00f… 89a8… 14:02:00                 1        16.1       1.4       2.2
#>  3 89a8100c00f… 89a8… 14:02:00                 2        16.1       1.4       2.2
#>  4 89a8100c00f… 89a8… 14:00:00                 1        14.7       1.3       1.9
#>  5 89a8100c00f… 89a8… 14:00:00                 2        14.7       1.3       1.9
#>  6 89a8100c00f… 89a8… 14:00:00                 3        14.7       2.3       1.9
#>  7 89a8100c00f… 89a8… 14:00:00                 4        14.7       2.4       1.9
#>  8 89a8100c00f… 89a8… 14:01:00                 1        14.7       1.3       1.9
#>  9 89a8100c00f… 89a8… 14:01:00                 2        14.7       2.5       1.9
#> 10 89a8100c00f… 89a8… 14:01:00                 3        14.7       2.5       1.9
#> # ℹ 5 more variables: transfer_time <dbl>, egress_time <dbl>, routes <chr>,
#> #   n_rides <int>, total_time <dbl>

A row is one departure minute of one origin-destination pair. This feed is frequency-based, so each minute has draws_per_minute rows (5 by default), one per simulated schedule; with a timetable-based feed there is one row per minute. Within a minute the draws are sorted by total time and numbered, so draw_number is a rank (1 is the fastest draw), not the order in which the draws were made.

With breakdown = TRUE each trip is split into minutes of access_time (walk to the first stop), wait_time, ride_time, transfer_time (walks between vehicles) and egress_time, plus the routes taken (GTFS route_ids joined by |, or [WALK] for a trip on foot) and n_rides. Every time is in minutes with one decimal, and total_time is the sum of the rounded parts:

t <- subset(trips, routes != "[WALK]")[1, ]
with(t, c(sum = access_time + wait_time + ride_time + transfer_time + egress_time,
          total_time = total_time))
#>        sum total_time 
#>       22.2       22.2

Trips longer than max_trip_duration keep their row with NA times.

The latest trip that arrives in time

arrival_travel_time_matrix() takes an arrival_datetime instead of a departure. It searches departures minute by minute over the max_trip_duration minutes before the arrival (the window may start on the previous day) and, for each pair, keeps the first trip, from the latest departure backwards, that arrives by the arrival time.

arrive <- arrival_travel_time_matrix(
  network, points[1:2, ], points,
  mode = c("WALK", "TRANSIT"),
  arrival_datetime = as.POSIXct("2019-05-13 15:00:00", tz = "America/Sao_Paulo"),
  max_trip_duration = 30,
  breakdown = TRUE,
  seed = 42,
  n_threads = 2
)
head(arrive)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 12
#>   from_id       to_id departure_time draw_number access_time wait_time ride_time
#>   <chr>         <chr> <chr>                <int>       <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 89a8100c00ff… 89a8… 14:59:00                 1           0         0         0
#> 2 89a8100c00ff… 89a8… 14:52:00                 1           0         0         0
#> 3 89a8100c00ff… 89a8… 14:49:00                 1           0         0         0
#> 4 89a8100c00ff… 89a8… 14:51:00                 1           0         0         0
#> 5 89a8100c00ff… 89a8… 14:46:00                 1           0         0         0
#> 6 89a8100c00ff… 89a8… 14:36:00                 1           0         0         0
#> # ℹ 5 more variables: transfer_time <dbl>, egress_time <dbl>, routes <chr>,
#> #   n_rides <int>, total_time <dbl>

There is at most one row per pair; pairs that cannot arrive in time are absent.

Limits

These functions keep the path of every trip and accept at most 5,000 destinations. The expanded matrix grows with origins × destinations × minutes × draws, so it is meant for a few origins at a time.
